Name: Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox
Description: Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox is an Assistant Professor of Computational Linguistics and the director of PICoL. He is interested in how we learn language from limited inputs and how we process it in real-time.

Name: Tatsua Aoyama
Description: Tatsuya completed his PhD in 2025. He is currently a research scientist at Meta AI

Name: Wes Scivetti
Description: Wesley Scivetti is a 3rd year Ph.D. candidate in Computational Linguistics. His research centers on the linguistic interpretability of language models, with particular focus on using Construction Grammar to understand language model performance.

Name: Kohei Kajikawa
Description: Kohei is a second-year PhD student. His research lies at the intersection of psycholinguistics and computational linguistics. He investigates human sentence processing through the lens of information theory and syntactic structures.

Name: Lanni Bu
Description: Lanni is currently a PhD student at The Ohio State University, working with WIlliam Schuler

Name: Xiulin Yang
Description: Xiulin Yang is a third-year PhD student. Her research interests include language modeling, language universals, (compositional) generalization of neural networks, LLMs, and semantics.

Name: Dan DeGenaro
Description: Dan DeGenaro is a rising 2nd-year PhD student in the CS department. He is interested in low-resource machine translation and speech recognition, multilingual NLP, and information-theoretic approaches to language modeling and linguistics

Name: Hyun Min
Description: Hyun is a third-year PhD student in the computational concentration from Busan, Korea. He is interested in robust representations of structure in language and how humans and statistical learners predict structure and resolve ambiguities.

Name: Devika Tiwari
Description: Devika Tiwari is a third-year PhD student in Computational Linguistics and Cognitive Science. She is interested in how we can use computational tools to understand how language is processed in the mind and brain. She is also working on topics in neurolinguistics and figurative language processing.

Name: Lauren Levine
Description: Lauren Levine is a PhD candidate, graduating, summer 2026. Her work focuses on linguistic annotation/resource creation, modeling for the task for bridging resolution, and investigating bridging with relation to LLMs and natural language reasoning.

Name: Lin Ai
Description: Lin is a 2nd year Master's student.
